name: health-export-mcp
author: Philip D'Souza
description: Query 190 Apple Health metrics from any MCP agent — zero-dependency, read-only, local-first.

tools.name: get_mcp_status
tools.description: Health check: data source, how many metrics/workouts are available, and the most recent data date. Call this first to confirm the bridge is connected.

tools.name: list_metrics
tools.description: List every available Apple Health metric with its unit, day count, and date range. Use this to discover metric names before querying.

tools.name: get_health_metrics
tools.description: Get daily values for a metric (or all metrics) over an optional date range, with an aggregate (avg/sum/min/max/latest). The core data-retrieval tool.

metric.description: Metric name, e.g. step_count, heart_rate, sleep_analysis. Omit to return every available metric.

start.description: Start of the date range (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the earliest available data.

end.description: End of the date range (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the most recent available data.

aggregation.description: How to reduce each day's samples to one value: avg, sum, min, max, or latest. Defaults to avg.

tools.name: get_trends
tools.description: Compare the most recent N-day window against the prior N days for a metric — returns change, percent change and direction (up/down/flat).

metric.description: Metric name to analyze the trend for, e.g. heart_rate, step_count, hrv.

window.description: Number of days in each comparison window (default 7): the most recent N days are compared against the prior N days.

tools.name: compare_periods
tools.description: Compare a metric between two arbitrary date periods (A vs B) — returns each aggregate plus the change and percent change.

metric.description: Metric name to compare across the two periods, e.g. resting_heart_rate, step_count.

periodA.description: The first date range to compare (the baseline period).

start.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

end.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

periodB.description: The second date range, compared against period A.

start.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

end.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

tools.name: get_structured_export
tools.description: Return clean structured JSON for the chosen metrics/date range — ideal to drop straight into an agent's context window.

metrics.description: Metric names to include, e.g. ["step_count","heart_rate"]. Omit to include every available metric.

start.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

end.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

tools.name: get_intraday
tools.description: The current hour-by-hour window from the iOS app's hourly automations (health-intraday.json, app 1.4+): hourly points plus latest value per metric. Replaced on every run — a live within-day view, not history.

metric.description: Metric name to filter, e.g. heart_rate. Omit for every metric in the window.

tools.name: query_health_data
tools.description: Natural-language convenience: pass a question (e.g. "average HRV last month") and get routed structured results. Prefer the specific tools above when you can.

question.description: A natural-language question about the health data, e.g. "average HRV last month" or "how did my steps trend this week".

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Logged context events from health-events.json: medication starts, habit changes, doctor visits, life events, shift blocks, episodes, travel. Optional type/tag/date filters; sorted ascending. Absence of the file means nothing was exported, not that nothing happened.

type.description: Event type, e.g. medication, habit, visit, life, shift, episode, travel, other.

start.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

end.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: The context fields the user explicitly opted in to sharing (health-profile.json), plus a presentFields list. An absent field was withheld or never enabled; absence must never be read as "none".

tools.name: get_workouts
tools.description: Query the workouts cache with activityType (name or raw HealthKit id), start, end filters and cursor pagination. Records return as stored, including avgHeartRate, running dynamics, intervals and hasRoute when exported; older caches simply lack those keys.

activityType.description: Activity name (e.g. Running) or raw HealthKit activity id (e.g. 37).

start.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

end.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's nextCursor.

tools.name: get_sleep_sessions
tools.description: Clustered sleep sessions from health-sessions.json, attributed to the WAKING day. Split nights are multiple sessions with the same day, returned as-is.

start.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

end.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

tools.name: get_cycle_context
tools.description: Day-in-cycle and coarse phase (follicular to the observed midpoint, luteal after) derived from logged period starts. Derived from logged periods only, never predictive.

date.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

tools.name: correlate_metrics
tools.description: Pearson correlation between two metrics' daily values with a 0 to 3 day lag (lag 1 pairs metricA on day d with metricB on the following day). r is withheld below 10 aligned pairs; every answer states association is not causation.

start.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).

end.description: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-03-14).
